In un paziente con tumore noto, noduli s:
In a patient with a known tumor, multiple hypoechoic solid nodules in the liver are metastases until proven otherwise. The ultrasound appearance of metastases varies: hypoechoic (the most common), "target" with a hypoechoic halo, hyperechoic (hypervascular tumors, carcinoid, colon) or cystic. In melanoma they are often multiple and hypoechoic.

Differential diagnosis: cysts are anechoic with posterior enhancement; typical hemangiomas are hyperechoic and well defined; focal steatosis and areas of focal sparing have typical locations and do not distort vessels. The next step is staging with contrast-enhanced CT or MRI and, if histological confirmation is needed, ultrasound-guided biopsy of the most accessible nodule, as in this exam.
